correctness.rationale: The odd-characteristic hyperelliptic quotient over F3 is P1, and choosing a rational infinity gives y^2=a f(x) with f monic squarefree of degree 9 or 10. These degrees account for 10 branch points, including infinity exactly in odd degree. The two leading square classes have identical counts over F9 and F81. The fresh census used exact quadratic characters and one or two points at infinity, respectively; it found 13,122 and 39,366 squarefree forms, with minimum B4 values 0 and 2. The sole zero is the monic degree-nine polynomial x^9−x, with N2=N4=10. Its two F3 twists are isomorphic by x↦−x, so the count is of F3 classes, not only presentations. Fresh replay: python3 /workspace/branches/471463d8-8bf5-404d-914a-b003b672463a/audit_record4.py; census.out alongside it records the full run. The supplied verification sources were inspected, not executed. In the family, the derivative is −1 and the smooth odd-degree model has genus (q^2−1)/2 and one rational infinity. For z=x^{q^2}−x≠0 in F_{q^4}, z^{q^2−1}=−1, so z^{(q^4−1)/2}=−1 because (q^2+1)/2 is odd. All remaining points are exactly the q^2 branch points from F_{q^2} and infinity. Thus 4B4=N4−N2=0. For all r≥5 one has q^{r/4}>1+sqrt(q^2−1): check q=3 directly and use q^{1/4}>1+1/q for q≥5. The universal positive closed-point criterion following Eq. (8) on p. 4 of arXiv:2310.11218 (just before Prop. 2.2) gives the upper threshold 5 for all curves, and the witness gives the lower threshold. This proves neither uniqueness outside the hyperelliptic locus nor a classification for other q.

evidence: For the F9 hyperelliptic quotient, an inert fiber at an F9 point would create two additional F81 points, forbidden by stability. Thus all 10 rational fibers are split or ramified; N=10 forces all 10 to be ramified. This is exactly the elementary split/ramified count used in the prior paper's p. 11 double-cover argument. Back over F3, put a rational base point at infinity. The branch set P1(F9) forces monic model polynomial x^9−x, and x↦−x identifies its two twists.

Put Q=q^2. Over F_{Q^2} the known maximal Hermitian curve, in the standard additive coordinates X^Q+X=Z^{Q+1}, maps onto the hyperelliptic Y^2=X^Q+X by Y=Z^{(Q+1)/2}. Maximality descends to this quotient (its H^1 is a subrepresentation). If b∈F_{Q^2}^* has b^Q=−b, then X↦bX changes X^Q−X to −b(X^Q+X), and −b is a nonsquare because (Q+1)/2 is odd. Thus the specified curve is the quadratic twist, with minimal F_{Q^2} count Q^2+1−Q(Q−1)=Q+1, also its branch-only F_Q count.
This familiar extremal-curve quotient and twist supplies the degree-four obstruction; the pre-existing universal criterion then gives the exact threshold.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: These deductions identify the actual subclass and the extremal witness in prior stronger inputs. The finite coefficient counts supply a correct replay of uniqueness, not a noncovered rigidity theorem. The all-q companion is a routine application of standard Hermitian quotient/twist arithmetic and the prior bound, not a new bound or a distinct obstruction.

value.rationale: An exact closed-point threshold and its exceptional curves are well motivated. Here the claimed inverse classification is determined by the prior exact stability candidates with a short standard double-cover count, while the infinite threshold follows from an extremal Hermitian quotient, its twist, and the known bound. The census usefully checks the arithmetic but its auxiliary counts of monic presentations are not a separate motivated invariant. No separately valuable unknown classification or threshold remains within the frozen result.
